previous_statement: Put h_1=(Ha^Q_{P,P})_1 and a_1=inf_{Z nonzero}||h_1(Z)||/||Z||. For each nonzero Z in S_P, validated nodes 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 specialized to n=1 give ||h_1(Z)||^2>=||h_1(Z^dagger dot Z)||-C_prod e||Z||^2. By the definition of a_1 and the level-one square estimate in the preceding child, this is at least ((1-K_sq e)a_1-C_prod e)||Z||^2. Divide by ||Z||^2 and take the infimum: because every norm ratio is nonnegative, inf_Z (||h_1(Z)||/||Z||)^2=a_1^2. Thus a_1^2>=(1-K_sq e)a_1-C_prod e, equivalently p(a_1)>=0.
new_statement: On the branch S_P != {0}, put h_1=(Ha^Q_{P,P})_1 and a_1=inf_{0 != Z in S_P} ||h_1(Z)||/||Z||. This is a finite nonnegative real because the indexing set is nonempty and consists of finite nonnegative norm ratios. For each nonzero Z in S_P, validated nodes 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 specialized to n=1 give ||h_1(Z)||^2 >= ||h_1(Z^dagger dot Z)||-C_prod e||Z||^2. The definition of a_1 (separating the cases Z^dagger dot Z=0 and !=0) and validated node 1.4.2.1.1 make the right side at least ((1-K_sq e)a_1-C_prod e)||Z||^2. Divide by ||Z||^2 and take the infimum. Since the ratios are nonnegative and their indexing set is nonempty, inf_Z (||h_1(Z)||/||Z||)^2=a_1^2. Hence a_1^2 >= (1-K_sq e)a_1-C_prod e, equivalently p(a_1)>=0 for p(t)=t^2-(1-K_sq e)t+C_prod e.
